To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
routing with uncertainty in wireless networks is a challenging task and that our SRCTP algorithm is a practical and effective solution to this problem.

the transient link uncertainties of wireless mesh networks (WMNs) can be explicitly modeled and considered in WMN routing, and a stochastic recoverable Canadian Traveller Problem based routing algorithm can be developed with practical implementation.
(1) WMN routing can be modeled as a recoverable Canadian Traveller problem, and (2) the optimal solution to this problem can be approximated using a simple online algorithm with a low probing cost.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) the intrinsic uncertainty of WMN routing; (2) the underlying connection between optimal routing with link uncertainty and CTP; (3) the design and implementation of a practical SRCTPs-based WMN routing algorithm.

the following questions: How can the transient link uncertainties in wireless links be explicitly addressed for routing in WMNs? How can routing algorithms be designed to explore the full potentials from WMN topologies, with low cost of probing?
a fundamental problem in WMN routing: how to achieve optimal routing under transient link uncertainties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed SRCTP routing algorithms can achieve a significant improvement over deterministic routing protocols.
the proposed SRCTP-based routing algorithm outperforms existing deterministic routing protocols in terms of end-to-end transmission delay and packet delivery ratio.

the proposed SRCTP algorithms are capable of exploring the full potentials of WMN routing, with explicit consideration on the transient link uncertainties, and can significantly outperform existing routing protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by explicitly accounting for transient link uncertainties at both PHY and MAC layers in WMN routing protocols, the full potentials of wireless multi-hop mesh can be explored.
, by exploiting the inherent link uncertainties, we have developed a novel routing protocol that can achieve significant performance improvement in WMNs.
we have developed a new routing paradigm with explicit consideration of the intrinsic uncertainties of wireless links.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with the uncertainty at the link level, routing in wireless mesh network can be significantly improved with online probing-based anypath forwarding.
, with explicit consideration on transient link uncertainties, the WMN routing performance can be improved significantly, which is of practical significance to the WMN community.
, by explicitly addressing link uncertainties, WMN routing can be made significantly more efficient.
